node_definition.done_when: Two live instances motivate this, both measured, each a run whose work was already merged and correct while the run itself sat unreadable. One declared status 'done', sat stuck for two days across two sessions, and held a claim that later refused an unrelated promotion in a third. Another declared status 'ready-for-review' in a peer project, where a coordinator nearly filed a false defect over it. In both cases the reader refuses the WHOLE manifest over that one field, so the classifier reports the run with the same word it uses for a corrupt file. Reproduce before repairing: parse_manifest on a manifest well-formed except for status 'done' refuses today, so quote the exact message you get. Then make the refusal carry what a reader needs to act: which field was rejected, the value it held, and the fact that the remainder parsed. DO NOT WIDEN THE STATUS VOCABULARY. Whether 'done' should be accepted is an open design decision on this plan and is not yours to settle; a node that quietly admits it would close that decision by implementation while leaving the reported defect untouched. The property under test belongs to the refusal, never to the vocabulary. Falsifier, which must fail at base: a case constructing both a manifest whose only defect is an unrecognised status word and a structurally broken manifest, requiring the two errors to differ, with the first naming the field and its offending value. Range it over the input domain rather than over the two words seen so far, so any unrecognised status is covered. Positive controls, all required: every currently recognised status still parses to itself, a genuinely malformed manifest still refuses, and no emitted message names a plan, a sprint or a run id. Gate: PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/ITER/mcintos/Code/reckon/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q tests/test_manifest_parse_format.py tests/test_manifest_nested_keys.py plus every tests file asserting on reports.py, captured to one log and reported as added failures against your base sha rather than as an absolute green, because that cohort carries pre-existing failures.
node_definition.goal: A reader can tell a manifest refused over one unrecognised field from a manifest that is genuinely unparseable.

runs.outcome: A manifest refused over one unrecognised field now names the field, the value it held, and that the remainder parsed, so a mis-stated run is distinguishable from a corrupt one: 'refused manifest: field status rejected value done...' against 'cannot read manifest: the body is present but no key: value field could be read'. The status vocabulary is unchanged, which the brief required because whether 'done' should be accepted is an open decision. Review 98/100. Its one finding is correct and I closed it rather than carrying it: the recorded gate omitted tests/test_crew_recovery.py, which imports the reader. Run at the node's base it gives 2 failed 89 passed and at its head 1 failed 90 passed, so the omitted file carries no added failure and one fewer. The process finding stands, the consequence is benign.

node_definition.done_when: Confirm the defect first and quote both the source line and your own population figure in the manifest. reckon/crew/dispatch.py writes 'session_reuse': bool(backend.get('session_reuse')) at lines 3175 and 4351, copying the BACKEND CONFIG FLAG onto the run record. RE-MEASURE IT YOURSELF rather than trusting those numbers, because the population moves and a figure quoted from a document is exactly the fuse this repository warns about. WHY IT MATTERS, and state this back in your own words: a coordinator diagnosing a dead worker reads session_reuse as evidence that a long-lived session was re-admitted, and it answers true whether or not anything was resumed. That happened here today and produced a confident wrong root cause which a peer fleet had to refute with three facts. A field that is always true is worse than an absent one, because a reader reaches for it and it answers. Repair so the record distinguishes what the backend PERMITS from what this run DID. A run resumed when its own launch carried a prior session into argv; it did not when it minted a fresh one, which its first system init line shows. Keep the capability visible if it is useful, but not under a name a reader will take for an observation. Falsifier, which must fail at base: a run launched without a prior session reports that it did not resume, while a run launched with one reports that it did, asserted on the record rather than on the config. Range over the domain rather than one backend: a backend permitting reuse with no prior session, the same backend with one, and a backend not permitting it. Positive controls: the dispatch path is otherwise unchanged, a member's captured session is still recorded where it already is, and no existing reader of the run record breaks. So the defect is the block-continuation test at reckon/crew/reports.py around line 302, which treats ANY indented line as continuing an open block; when the fields are themselves indented, every field after a block-scalar one is folded into its value. A repair landed hours ago closing a different route to the same loss, and its own docstring around line 250 says the least-indented-column rule exists to preserve exactly this case, so the documented intent and the behaviour disagree. Repair so a block scalar ends when a line appears at or left of the column where the fields themselves sit, rather than at column zero. Positive controls, all required: every case in tests/test_manifest_nested_keys.py and tests/test_manifest_parse_format.py still passes, an ordinary unindented manifest is unchanged, and a genuine multi-line block scalar still keeps all of its own lines. A reader then sees a failing doccheck test caused by an edit to an unrelated document. Read the repository rule forbidding a test that encodes a moving value before you start; this is that rule with a document in place of a number. Repair so the assertion owns its specimen: a fixture carrying the shapes that motivated the exclusion, which are a literal asterisk pair inside a pre block, one inside a code span, and at least one in genuine prose in the same document so the test still separates the two outcomes. Falsifier, demonstrated in both halves rather than asserted: adding a literal asterisk pair to a comment body in docs/plans/crew-observability-truth.html leaves this test file passing, and adding the same to the fixture's prose makes it fail. Show the two runs. Positive controls: every other case in the file passes unchanged, and the exclusion is still exercised against real quoted content rather than only synthetic input. You may keep a live-document check if it is insensitive to that plan's content, and if you keep one, state in the manifest what edit to that plan would break it. node_definition.done_when: Establish the gap before repairing it and quote your findings in the manifest. Across the crew command surface, --write-path appears on dispatch alone: crew resume takes only run, advice, backend and reason, and no command narrows or releases a claim once dispatch has created it. Verify that yourself from the command help rather than trusting this sentence. The consequence measured here: a claim is created at dispatch and destroyed at promotion and cannot change in between, so every mid-flight scope movement lands on a coordinator as a hand edit to a live pointer under the crew config home. That happened in this session, and separately a run terminal since 2026-09-15 held a claim on a source file that refused an unrelated promotion two days later in a third session. Build the release path in reckon/crew/claims.py as the mechanism, and DO NOT wire a new command into reckon/cli.py: that file is outside your scope and a second node owns the surface. State in your manifest what the entry point should look like so the caller can add it. Falsifier, which must fail at base: a claim on a declared path can be released through the module, after which a second run may declare that same path without refusal, asserted by dispatching-equivalent claim checks rather than by reading the pointer file. Range over the domain: a claim released while its run is terminal, a claim narrowed from two paths to one, and a release attempted against a run whose process is still alive, which must REFUSE rather than succeed, because releasing a live worker's claim is how two workers end up writing one file. Positive controls, all required: an untouched claim still refuses a second writer, promotion still releases claims as it does today, and the existing exclusivity checks are unchanged. Build every fixture in a temp directory and assert the real crew config home is untouched afterwards, since this module writes there. Gate: PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/ITER/mcintos/Code/reckon/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q your new file plus tests/test_crew_cross_project_claims.py tests/test_crew_dispatch_guard.py tests/test_crew.py, captured to one log and reported as added failures against your base sha rather than as an absolute green; that cohort carries pre-existing failures.

node_definition.done_when: A peer project lost its entire roster to a silent write: 87 members to 0 at commit 490b5cc5, in a promote commit, exit 0, nothing reported. It surfaced six hours later as a dispatch refused for a member the coordinator had registered and used earlier the same session, and member add then rebuilt from zero, so the repair mechanism became a second writer of the corrupted state. Runs and holds in the same document survived. THE MECHANISM IS NOT KNOWN and you are not being asked to find it. Four candidates were ruled out here already, and record in your manifest that you did not re-derive them: the envelope loader raises on a corrupt file rather than defaulting, all four ledger.write callers pass a dict that preserves members, write refuses a stale expected_version, and no module outside ledger.py writes that document. Build the guard instead, because it is correct whether or not the cause is ever found. Refuse a write whose member count is lower than the member count of the version it is replacing, unless the caller states an intent to remove. Add that intent as an explicit parameter so a genuine removal stays possible and is visible at the call site. Falsifier, which must fail at base: a write carrying fewer members than the stored state raises rather than succeeding, and the stored roster is unchanged afterwards. Range over the domain rather than the 87-to-0 case: a drop to zero, a drop of one, a drop combined with an addition so the net is negative, and a same-count write that replaces one member with another, which must be REFUSED too if your rule is count-only, so decide whether identity or count is the thing guarded and say which you chose and why. Positive controls, all required: an ordinary registration that adds a member still succeeds, a re-registration of an existing member still succeeds, an explicit removal with the new intent parameter succeeds, and a write to a project with no ledger yet still creates one from empty without tripping the guard, since an absent ledger legitimately has zero members. Build every fixture in a temp directory and assert the real crew config home and the real docs directories are untouched. Gate: PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/ITER/mcintos/Code/reckon/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q your new file plus tests/test_ledger.py tests/test_roster_write_commits.py tests/test_crew_members.py tests/test_crew.py, captured to one log and reported as added failures against your base sha rather than as an absolute green; that cohort carries pre-existing failures.
node_definition.goal: A ledger write that would reduce the roster without being asked to is refused.

node_definition.done_when: Author tests/test_report_only_promotion.py. It synthesises a temporary repository and pointer under tmp_path and never reads or writes the real crew home, asserting afterwards that the real pointer directory is untouched. Four cases, all holding at the repaired head. (a) A run whose manifest is status complete, commits empty, and whose changed_paths name only absolute paths outside the repository root promotes through the same entry point 'reckon crew complete' reaches, instead of raising the missing-commit refusal. (b) A manifest naming one path under the repository root with no commits is STILL refused with that message. (c) A mixed manifest naming one in-repository path beside out-of-repository paths is still refused, because the in-repository path still needs its commit. (d) A path written absolutely that resolves under the repository root counts as inside, so the test cannot pass by string-matching any particular directory name. Run the new file at base FIRST and quote in the manifest which cases fail there. Case (a) must fail at base, or the test does not measure the defect and the node is not done. Then repair reckon/crew/promotion.py so the guard's question is whether any changed path resolves under the run's repository root, leaving the existing prose-none behaviour unchanged. Gate: PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/ITER/mcintos/Code/reckon/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q tests/test_report_only_promotion.py tests/test_crew_promotion.py tests/test_crew_promotion_scope.py tests/test_crew_test_role.py, recorded at base and at head with no added failures. A change that makes case (b) or (c) promote is a failure, not a pass.

node_definition.done_when: the review for r-20260917T165959552736-the-arrival-is-the-first-row-for-a-node parses all five score dimensions. That run built a canonical extraction for which watch rows are real arrivals, because three fleets wrote three filters over the same logs and got three answers. Judge whether the discriminator is first appearance per node rather than event class, since filtering on transition drops genuine arrivals recorded as baseline while accepting all baseline rows re-counts a follower's re-inventory. Judge the stamps too: the event files are mixed format, carrying rendered rows in local time beside JSON rows, so confirm every returned stamp is UTC explicitly and that a row whose zone cannot be established reports unknown rather than being assumed. A coordinator merging the two naively today manufactured a descending limb out of a concurrent ascent.

node_definition.done_when: Three fleets wrote three different filters over the same watch logs this week and got different answers, which is the defect. Establish the two failure modes yourself from the data before building: read the event files under ~/.config/reckon/crew/watch/ and confirm both halves. Filtering on event equal to transition DROPS genuine arrivals, because a dispatch a follower first sees is recorded as baseline with a null from_state, having no prior state to transition from; a peer fleet measured three real dispatches lost this way and came close to telling another fleet its own self-report was wrong. Accepting every baseline row INVENTS arrivals, because a follower re-attaching re-inventories the whole fleet and emits one row per live run within the same second. The correct discriminator is FIRST APPEARANCE PER NODE, not event class: the earliest row for a node is its arrival whatever its class, later baseline rows for that node are re-inventory, and transitions after the first row are real state changes. Build that as a reusable extraction in reckon/crew/query.py returning arrivals and state changes with their stamps. DO NOT wire a command into reckon/cli.py: that file is outside your scope, and state in the manifest what the entry point should look like so the caller can add it. STAMPS ARE THE OTHER HALF OF THIS and are not optional: the event files are mixed-format, carrying rendered ticker rows in LOCAL time alongside JSON rows, and a coordinator merging the two naively today manufactured a descending limb out of a concurrent ascent. Every stamp your extraction returns is UTC, explicitly, and a row whose zone cannot be established is reported as unknown rather than assumed. Falsifier, which must fail at base: over a fixture carrying a follower restart, the extraction returns each node exactly once as an arrival and no re-inventory row is counted, while a genuine dispatch recorded as baseline IS counted. Range over the domain rather than one file: a node appearing first as baseline, first as transition, appearing in two separate follower sessions, and a node whose only row is a re-inventory. Positive controls: real state changes after the first row are preserved in order, and a file with no baseline rows at all yields the same arrivals it does today. Gate: PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/ITER/mcintos/Code/reckon/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q your new file plus tests/test_crew_watch_stream.py tests/test_follow_observes_other_sessions.py tests/test_crew_monitor_output.py, captured to one log and reported as added failures against your base sha rather than as an absolute green.

node_definition.done_when: Reproduce first and paste the figures into the manifest. At the current head reckon.ledger.load returns an empty store at version 0 for an absent path, because an absent ledger is read as a project that has run no workers yet. A promotion preparing a write against that reading computes current_view as expected_version 0 equalling stored_version 0, so the roster guard finds nothing to drop against an empty roster and the run-count guard compares one incoming row against zero stored rows and passes. Show it: point a write at a path that does not exist and show it succeeds at version 1, beside the same code correctly refusing to shrink a real store of 1267 runs when the view is current. Then tests/test_a_promotion_never_creates_a_ledger.py passes and asserts three things. A promotion write that finds no ledger file at the resolved path is refused with a LedgerError naming the run store as the independent authority that holds every promoted run, rather than creating a store. Initialising a genuinely new project's ledger remains possible through an explicit argument that says so, asserted by calling that path and getting a store, so initialising is a deliberate act rather than a fallback from absence. And an envelope whose members or runs key is not a list is refused rather than silently read as an empty project, asserted against such a file, because that fallback collapses a malformed read into a fresh start in the same way. Ruff check and format over exactly the staged paths add no findings beyond the same paths at the base revision, with both counts pasted as digits. A logged live composition of a fenced clive launch plan shows settings.json with the operator's Stop hook command under its CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. The declared negative control is executed and logged. The gate adds no failures over tests/test_fenced_resume_reaches_its_harness.py, tests/test_crew_dispatch_resume.py, tests/test_every_attempt_is_supervised.py and tests/test_flight.py against the base. The evidence record carries an anchor with a table of what each dialect's declaration carries.
node_definition.goal: Make a fenced run's harness home carry the operator-home files that its backend declares its harness reads, so hooks, instruction files and harness configuration survive the fence for any harness, as flight configuration rather than per-dialect code. Today seed_harness_home in reckon/_backends.py creates an empty directory, so since e4933730 fenced claude and clive workers load no ~/.claude/settings.json hooks (the worker Stop hook, native_agent_guard.py, shell_function_recursion_guard.py) and no user CLAUDE.md. A fenced codex worker would lose ~/.codex/AGENTS.md (codex reads AGENTS.md, never CLAUDE.md), config.toml and rules/. A resume cannot find a session recorded in the operator home: resuming r-20260925T062408975588-fenced-workers-smoke at 18:46 exited with 'No conversation found with session ID eb46c4e0-0ac6-4891-b9b6-6fd5fb4773e4'. What a worker loads is decided by its harness, not its model: clive runs the claude harness in front of several open-weight models, and AGENTS.md is the emerging standard for non-claude harnesses. So the file list lives in each backend's flight entry, with shipped defaults per dialect. node_definition.done_when: reckon/crew/review.py derives, for every review it stores, an added-failures-by-id count from the reviewed run's own base and head gate logs. The count is the pytest node ids reported FAILED or ERROR in the head log that do not appear in the base log, read from the files the reviewed manifest names. The count and the added ids are stored on the review record. When the count is nonzero, the stored total is capped at a threshold below the promotion floor the promotion path already reads, and the record says why, unless the reviewed node's done-when or manifest explicitly retires those test ids by name. When the manifest names no base log or no head log, the record says the count is unmeasured, rather than zero, and does not cap. tests/test_review_counts_added_failures.py synthesises a reviewed run in tmp_path (the pytest fixture) whose base log fails test ids A and B, and whose head log fails B, C and D. It asserts the stored record carries count 2 with ids C and D, and a total at or below the cap. A second case has the same logs and a done-when retiring C and D, and asserts no cap. A third case has no base log, and asserts the count is recorded as unmeasured and not zero. The negative control computes the count as head failures minus base failures by number rather than by id, and the first case must fail, because 3 minus 2 is 1, not 2. reckon/crew/recovery.py is not edited. tests/test_crew_review.py and any existing review test files add no failures against the base, with pytest basetemp outside any git repository. Gate and control logs are written under the run directory. The change is committed in this worktree.

node_definition.done_when:
Two defects in the fenced launch composition in reckon/_backends.py are fixed.

(1) _declared_write_grant resolves a declared write path that is not absolute against the WORKTREE when a worktree is given. A repo-relative path names a file in the worker's own checkout, so it lies inside the worktree and is skipped. It must never be joined to the repository argument, which is the main checkout. Only an absolute declared path can produce a grant outside the worktree. Measured today: node declarations such as reckon/crew/x.py produced --bind ~/Code/reckon/reckon, ~/Code/reckon/tests and ~/Code/reckon/docs/plans in fenced argv, re-opening the main checkout the fence exists to seal. The tests use a synthesised repository and a detached worktree under tmp_path (the pytest fixture), with every crew directory environment-resolved to tmp_path. Compose a fenced launch plan through the production path, launch_plan, with fence roots from fenced_write_roots, for a worktree-full backend whose node declares reckon/crew/x.py, tests/test_x.py and docs/plans/p.html. Assert no --bind destination lies under the repository root except that worktree's own .git/worktrees directory entry for that worktree and the shared .git/objects. Negative control: resolve against the repository again; the no-main-checkout-bind assertion must fail.

(2) When fenced, every write root including the manifest's parent directory is created BEFORE the harness home is resolved and seeded. A manifest declared in a directory that does not exist yet then still gets its harness home and its CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR or CODEX_HOME. Measured today: codex-luna run r-20260926T191902635940 had its manifest in a missing directory. No harness home was seeded, codex fell back to the read-only ~/.codex, and it exited 1 with "failed to initialize in-process app-server client: Read-only file system". node_definition.done_when: A resumed run is never classified stalled on the quiet time of a stream from an earlier attempt. The classifier in reckon/crew/recovery.py measures a live run's quiet time from the later of two things: the current attempt's own launch time, and the last write to that attempt's own log. Before the current attempt's log exists, the run reads working within the same launch-window grace a fresh dispatch gets. Measured on 2026-09-26: watcher-seat-survives-other-hosts rendered complete → stalled ("stream quiet for 956s") at 20:26:34 local, 20 s after `crew resume`, because resume-1.jsonl did not exist yet and the classifier aged the run from the previous stream.jsonl. It recovered at 20:26:55. tests/test_resume_is_aged_from_its_own_start.py synthesises a live run record in tmp_path (the pytest fixture), with every crew directory environment-resolved to tmp_path and a live stub pid. Its stream.jsonl was last written 1000 s ago. It has just been resumed: the attempt was launched 5 s ago, and resume-1.jsonl is absent. The test asserts the classification is not stalled. A second case has the attempt's log last written 1000 s ago, and asserts stalled, so the guard still fires on a genuinely quiet resume. Negative control: age from the earliest stream again; the first case must fail. tests/test_crew_recovery.py adds no failures against the base, with pytest basetemp outside any git repository. Gate and control logs are written under the run directory. The change is committed in this worktree.
node_definition.goal: Make the classifier age a resumed run from its own attempt, never from an earlier attempt's stream.

node_definition.done_when:
A follower re-armed on another host of the same shared filesystem continues from its checkpoint instead of replaying the stream. Measured on 2026-09-27 after clu-2058 failed: s23-coord's checkpoint recorded stream_identity {dev: 42, ino: 4299543955}. From clu-2020 the same stream stats as dev 44 with the same inode, because GPFS gives the mount a different device number on each client node. follow_checkpoint.continues() in reckon/crew/follow_checkpoint.py compares dev and ino, returns False, and the follower re-reads the whole stream as unseen. It then emits days of history as transitions, including promoted → dispatched, plus rows for other sessions despite --session. The harness stopped the monitors of s21, s23 and s25 for output volume.

(1) Stream identity survives a host change. Either drop st_dev from the comparison, or stamp the stream with an identity token written when the stream is created and compare that. Say which in the commit. A genuinely replaced stream (a new inode at the same path, or a new token) still falls back.
(2) A follower arm with no continuable checkpoint emits baseline rows for everything before its arm time and zero transition rows.
(3) The --session filter applies on every path, replay and baseline included, so no row for another session is emitted.

tests/test_follower_survives_a_host_change.py, in tmp_path (the pytest fixture) with every crew directory environment-resolved to tmp_path:
- A checkpoint whose recorded dev differs from the stream's current dev while the inode matches continues.
- A replaced stream (new inode) does not continue.
- An arm on a synthesised stream holding earlier transitions for two sessions, with no checkpoint, yields zero transition rows and zero rows for the other session.
Negative control: today's dev-and-ino comparison; the host-change case must fail.
tests/test_follow_rearm_continues.py and tests/test_follower_keeps_memory_and_idles_quietly.py add no failures against the base, with pytest basetemp outside any git repository. Gate and control logs are written under the run directory, each headed with revision, tree and the literal command. The manifest's baseline_suite and after_suite are either a JSON object with log_path and failure_ids or absent. The change is committed in this worktree.

A fenced codex run can persist a refreshed login, so the first token refresh no longer burns the shared login. Measured on 2026-09-27: every fenced codex run gets the operator's single /home/ITER/mcintos/.codex/auth.json bound read-only at CODEX_HOME/auth.json (reckon/_backends.py, _harness_credential_binds). That file was last written 2026-09-17. codex-luna run r-20260926T204353115391 then failed with "Your access token could not be refreshed because your refresh token was already used" and a 401. The explanation: OAuth refresh tokens are single-use, and a fenced refresh rotated the token server-side but could not write it back. The lead chose to bind ONLY that one file read-write; the rest of ~/.codex stays sealed.

Step 1 is measure first. Establish how the installed codex binary (/home/ITER/mcintos/.npm/packages/bin/codex) writes auth.json on refresh: in place (open with O_TRUNC or O_WRONLY on the same inode) or by writing a temp file and renaming it over auth.json. Rename onto a file bind mount fails with EBUSY or EXDEV inside bubblewrap. Use strace -f -e trace=openat,rename,renameat,renameat2 on a codex command that rewrites auth.json, for example a login status or refresh path, run against a COPY of auth.json in a scratch CODEX_HOME under tmp_path. Never run it against the real ~/.codex, and never trigger a real refresh of the operator's token. Record the syscalls in logs/codex-auth-write-mode.log. If no command rewrites auth.json without a real refresh, say so and use the codex source or docs to establish the write mode, citing it.

Step 2: if the write is in place, change the fence so CODEX_HOME/auth.json is a read-write bind of /home/ITER/mcintos/.codex/auth.json, and the protected read-only overlay of ~/.codex stays in force for every other path. If the write is a rename, do not change the bind. Write status: blocked with the measurement, because the lead must then choose another design.

Tests, in tests/test_fenced_codex_can_persist_its_login.py, in tmp_path (the pytest fixture) with a synthesised operator home:
- The composed fenced argv for a codex backend carries a read-write bind (--bind, not --ro-bind) for the operator auth.json at CODEX_HOME/auth.json.
- It still carries the read-only protection for the rest of the operator's ~/.codex.
- No copy of auth.json is ever written into the run directory.
Negative control: restore --ro-bind; the first assertion must fail.
tests/test_each_run_owns_its_harness_home.py, tests/test_fence_never_binds_the_main_checkout.py and tests/test_fence_is_on_again.py add no failures against the base, with pytest basetemp outside any git repository. Logs go under the run directory, each headed with revision, tree and the literal command. The change is committed in this worktree.

node_definition.done_when:
Measured 2026-09-28 on reckon main at 1b44f63e, after the host-change fix. Four coordinators see a re-armed `reckon crew follow` replay rows it already delivered. Each arming runs under a harness Monitor, and a Monitor stops its follower at a 29-minute expiry, the way a SIGTERM would. Two patterns:

A. Same-session window, repeated on every re-arm, now measured by s23-coord. The re-emitted rows are exactly the contents of the follower's pane-history file, e.g. ~/.config/reckon/crew/watch/reckon-18dc8a86709b.followers/s23-coord-b61cfdd0f295.history.json. It is re-printed by _follow_history_burst (reckon/cli.py, around line 2869, called near line 3206, capped at 100 rows and 4 h). Since the re-arm banners were removed on 26 Sep it prints unframed, so a consumer reads it as new transitions. The checkpoint itself continues correctly. Evidence: s21's re-arms at about 08:18 and 08:47 local both began at the row stamped 06:43:21. s22's four re-arms (07:45, 08:05, 08:18, 08:41) all began at 06:55:16. s22's --run filters did not suppress it.

B. Cross-session, hours-long replay, not yet explained. s25-coord's re-arm at about 08:59 local opened at 22:43:58 the previous evening (n-promotion-commit-resolution -> dispatched) and re-emitted hours of transitions, mostly other sessions' runs despite --session s25-coord. Its earlier re-arms at 06:48 and 07:57 did the same. This exceeds the burst's 4 h cap, so it is a different path: a checkpoint that did not continue, a baseline or seed path that ignores --session, or something else. Read s25's checkpoint and history, ~/.config/reckon/crew/watch/reckon-18dc8a86709b.followers/s25-coord-2b86c22ac91e.checkpoint.json and its .history.json, only; never write them.

(1) Diagnose both patterns by reading the real stream ~/.config/reckon/crew/watch/reckon-18dc8a86709b.events and the followers' checkpoint and history files, never writing any of them. State each mechanism in the commit message and the manifest.
(2) Fix, following this decision. A re-arm never presents already-delivered history as new transitions. When stdout is not a TTY (the Monitor case), the history burst is not printed at all. When stdout is a TTY, the burst is printed under one dim frame line naming it as earlier history. The --session and --run filters hold on every path: replay, baseline, seed and burst. A re-arm emits exactly the transitions appended after the previous arm's delivered position, once each.
(3) tests/test_follower_rearm_shows_nothing_twice.py runs in tmp_path (the pytest fixture), with every crew directory environment-resolved to tmp_path, and afterwards asserts that the real ~/.config/reckon/crew/watch is untouched. Cases:
- non-TTY re-arm after a stop without the clean-exit path, with nothing new: zero rows;
- the same, with new transitions appended before the re-arm: exactly the new rows;
- TTY re-arm: the burst appears only under its frame line;
- a stream holding another session's transitions, plus the pattern-B precondition you diagnose: zero rows for the other session;
- a run that flapped stalled/blocked and was discarded before the stop: not re-emitted.
Negative control: today's code. The first case must fail.
(4) tests/test_follow_rearm_continues.py, tests/test_follower_keeps_memory.py, tests/test_follower_keeps_memory_and_idles_quietly.py, tests/test_follower_survives_a_host_change.py and tests/test_ticker_row_is_one_transition.py add no failures against the base, with pytest basetemp outside any git repository. baseline_suite and after_suite in the manifest are JSON objects with log_path and failure_ids.
Gate, control and neighbour logs are written under the run directory, each headed with the revision, the tree and the literal command. The gate command names the absolute .venv python. Commit in this worktree. Tests are fast and this runs on the fleet node, so run them in place.

Peer: s23-coord's node follower-prints-only-policy-rows is concurrently changing the follower's row path in reckon/cli.py and reckon/crew/ticker.py. Keep your cli.py change confined to the history burst, re-arm and filter paths, and do not reformat or move surrounding code. The coordinator merges both in a scratch worktree. If pattern B's fix needs a file outside your write paths, stop and name it in the manifest's blockers.

node_definition.done_when: reckon/velocity.py reports, per lane and day, the share of all dispatches that continued another task's session. A dispatch continued another task's session when its recorded session_id equals that of an earlier run whose (project, plan, node) differs. The denominator is every dispatch in that lane and day, as the plan's section s4 says. The lane comes from the existing lane() function, not a second family list. A dispatch with no recorded session_id is counted as unmeasured beside the share, never as fresh. tests/test_velocity_session_continuity.py synthesises run rows: a same-task resume, which is not counted; a cross-task continuation, which is counted; a missing session_id, which is counted unmeasured; and two lanes on two days. It asserts the per-lane-day shares and passes at exit 0, as does tests/test_velocity.py. A recorded measurement, which is not a test, runs the reading over reckon's committed run records for 2026-09-20 to 2026-09-27. It logs the per-lane-day shares, and states beside them the before and after figures in docs/research/data/codex-resume-burn.json and codex-resume-burn-after.json with any disagreement explained. The manifest cites that log. The manifest records base and head arms of the two test files, each log header printing its revision and reckon.__file__, and cites the reuse map at /home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/reports/reckon/s25-coord/s25-reuse-map-quota-runway/reuse-map.md section 4 for lane, capture_project and measure, re-derived at its own base. The declared negative control is applied, the same-task case is observed to fail, and that log's absolute path is in the manifest with an EXIT= line and the FAILED test id.

A behaviour with code but no passing test that asserts it is partly-done, not done.
- partly-done: what landed (with the evidence above) and exactly what is missing.
- still-required: what is missing at the revision, concretely (the function, file or test that does not exist or does not do it), and whether the item's stated premise still holds at the revision.
- superseded: the landed mechanism that replaced it (commit sha and file), and why the item's goal is met or moot.
- stale-wording: the item is still wanted but its text names something that no longer exists or has moved; say what it should name.

Tests are fast and you are on the fleet node, so run them in place, bounded to the test files you cite. Stop once both files are written and the manifest reads complete.

A second case, where the document omits waiting, asserts the payload marks it unknown, not 0. Both fail at the base revision, which carries none of these fields (logged), and pass at the head. The negative control drops the counts from the carried reading in a scratch copy, and the first case fails, with the mutation on the red log's first line and an EXIT= line after pytest's output. The gate is the new test plus the existing test files that exercise lane_reading. It exits 0, or shows no added failing ids against the base, with both arms recorded as log paths under baseline_suite and after_suite. The test neither reads nor writes the real lane document or ~/.config/reckon.
node_definition.goal: Plan crew-observability-truth §22: the lane reading is sufficient to route. Read the section in docs/plans/crew-observability-truth.html. The dispatch payload's lane_reading is composed near reckon/crew/dispatch.py:2490-2614 and always emitted near :2037. It carries headroom, binding_observed, mean_context, observed_at, age and shelf life. It does not carry the lane's generating and waiting counts, or the achieved throughput with its age and its denominator. Make lane_reading carry those, read from the lane document the dispatch already consults (~/public/imas-ambix/lane.json or its configured equivalent), so that a dispatcher can choose a lane without a second read. A count the document does not publish is carried as unknown, never as zero.

The keep budget: the lead has locked the limit at 25 pending plans and four batches of 17 cover 68, so this batch proposes at most 6 keeps, ranked by live, unfinished work, where a live run counts in a plan's favour. Every other plan is merge or close, with a reason saying why it is not in the top six. The first batch's accepted record is docs/evidence/archive/open-work-is-capped-landed.html section triage-first-batch; follow its columns. The node writes only its own evidence fragment and figure directory, edits no plan, names the main HEAD sha it read at in the fragment and the manifest, gives any figure XML-safe characters and parses it with ElementTree, and carries one landing: line in the manifest.

node_definition.done_when: reckon/resources.py treats docs/evidence/fragments/ as a known non-resource subtree. Every typed-resource discovery walk (the rglob sites in that module) skips it, and _path_context does not raise ResourceCollision for a path under evidence/fragments/. A mis-shaped path anywhere else under a typed root is still refused as today. The fragments stay readable by reckon.evidence.compose_landed_record, which reads them directly. tests/test_discovery_skips_evidence_fragments.py builds a synthesised docs tree under tmp_path with two plans, a cumulative record and one fragment at docs/evidence/fragments/PLAN/NODE.html. It asserts that read_plan, through reckon.mcp's public read path, succeeds for both plans, including the plan the fragment does not belong to; that the composed record still contains the fragment's anchor; and that a mis-shaped non-fragment path such as docs/evidence/extra/x.html is still refused. It passes at exit 0, as do the existing resource and typed-resource test files the change reaches. The manifest records base and head arms of those files, each log header printing its revision and reckon.__file__, with FAILED ids per arm, and the read_plan case must fail at base. The declared negative control is applied, the unrelated-plan read_plan case is observed to fail, and that log's absolute path is in the manifest with an EXIT= line and the FAILED test id. This is a hotfix: other coordinators' merges are blocked until it lands, so keep it to this change.

node_definition.done_when: For each metered budget group and role, reckon/budget.py reports the runs remaining before the weekly reset. The figure is the group's remaining seven-day window divided by the mean per-run quota cost over the trailing seven days. The per-run cost is read from the committed run records' lane_receipt quota_windows, which carry a ten-thousand-and-eighty-minute window. The figure carries its own observation age, and it is unmeasured, never zero, when fewer than one priced run exists. The judgement extends _group_bar and group_pace rather than adding a second bar. The drain deadline comes from reckon/crew/pace.py, and group membership from budget_group.declared_groups; neither is restated. A wave whose projected cost, its node count times the mean per-run cost, exceeds the remaining window is refused, and the refusal names the runs remaining and the reset time. Exposing the figure on the command line is out of scope. tests/test_preflight_runs_remaining.py builds synthetic run records and a synthetic group window under tmp_path. It asserts the runs-remaining figure, the refusal of a wave projected past its reset with the runs-remaining figure and reset time in its text, admission of a wave inside the window, and unmeasured when no priced run exists. It passes at exit 0, as do the existing budget and pace test files the change reaches. The manifest records base and head arms of those files, each log header printing its revision and reckon.__file__, with FAILED ids per arm, and cites the reuse map at /home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/reports/reckon/s25-coord/s25-reuse-map-quota-runway/reuse-map.md section 1, re-derived at its own base. The declared negative control is applied, the past-reset wave is observed to be admitted, and that log's absolute path is in the manifest with an EXIT= line and the FAILED test id.

It writes the tier to the ledger row as review_tier. _require_review_waiver reads that tier in place of the role check: a none-tier run promotes without a stored review, and its ledger row records the tier as the reason no review exists. A full-tier or light-tier run without a stored review at the promoted head is refused exactly as today, and a review run stays exempt. node_definition.done_when: The node's evidence fragment holds one table row for each binding sentence in skills/reckon-build/references/conditional-guidance.md, effort-routing.md, lane-routing.md, outage-recovery.md, worker-backends.md, worker-protocol.md, worker-verification.md, orchestrator-harness/claude-code.md and orchestrator-harness/codex-cli.md, all under skills/reckon-build/references/, and no other file. Method: a binding sentence states a rule a coordinator or worker must follow; it contains or implies must, never, always, refuse, or an imperative. Every other sentence is counted but not rowed. Each row carries five things: the rule, quoted or tightly paraphrased with its file and line at main HEAD; whether code enforces it, naming the refusal or check by file and symbol; whether it is still wanted, proposed by you, since the lead confirms that column; one disposition, one of delete as enforced, keep, merge into a named surviving row, or delete as obsolete; and a one-line reason. A row marked enforced names a test that drives the guarded action far enough to make the refusal or check fire. That test is run in the FOREGROUND and its log is cited by absolute path under the run directory; a rule with no such test is not marked enforced. The fragment states the file's total sentence count beside its row count, so the scope of binding is visible, and names the main HEAD sha it read at. Nothing in the skill files or the code is edited. The node writes only its own evidence fragment and figure directory. Figures are XML-safe and parsed with ElementTree. The manifest carries one landing: line.

Two defects that reviews of landed nodes found in the shared helpers' callers are repaired.

1. reckon/_store.py:write_json_atomically. When the chmod that applies a requested mode raises, the empty sibling temporary it created stays on disk, although the module promises that a failure leaves neither a partial destination nor a stray sibling. Every failure after the temporary is created now removes it.
2. reckon/crew/query.py:_normalize_stamp and reckon/crew/rollout.py:_parse_timestamp. Both test whether a stamp states its zone with a predicate that accepts only a trailing Z or z, or an offset ending in minutes. So 2026-09-29T01:02:03+00:00:30, an offset carrying seconds, is read as naming no zone. query returns (None, "unknown") and rollout returns a naive datetime, where base c786e44a returned ("2026-09-29T01:01:33+00:00", "utc") and an aware 2026-09-29T01:01:33+00:00. The zone test reads the parsed result's tzinfo rather than the text's shape, and both outputs match base.

tests/test_shared_helper_edges.py covers both:
- A chmod that raises, patched in, leaves no file in the directory other than the untouched destination.
- The seconds-offset stamp gives the base outputs above for both callers.
The expectations are recorded at base cea6da07 by running the base code where they concern existing behaviour.

That file, tests/test_timestamp_callers_batch_a.py, tests/test_writer_callers_first_wave.py and tests/test_one_atomic_writer_and_number_decoder.py pass at exit 0. The head arm runs at the committed head. Every gate log opens with one line naming its revision, tree and command. The declared negative control is applied and observed to fail, and its log's absolute path is in the manifest with an EXIT= line and the FAILED id. The full project suite is not run by this node.

Case (a) fails at the base revision (logged) and passes at the head. A replay section in the manifest runs the new check read-only against the four named runs' real manifests and control logs, recording that each is now admitted, without writing to those run directories. The negative control, in a scratch copy, restores the baseline-only comparison; case (a) fails, with the mutation on the red log's first line and an EXIT= line after pytest's output. The gate is the new test plus every tests/ file whose name contains negative_control or control_gate; both arms are recorded as one JSON object each under baseline_suite and after_suite (revision, command, exit_status, one log_path, failure_ids), each log ending in an EXIT= line, with the head arm adding no failing id. ruff check plus ruff format --check on the changed paths add no finding against the base. The tests neither read nor write the real ~/.config/reckon.

- Any single data file above 300,000 bytes belongs in the run directory, not the repository.

It also asserts that a node whose done-when names a figure is told it may write the figure but not evidence prose. The existing prompt tests (tests/test_crew_prompts.py, tests/test_the_prompt_carries_the_evidence_contract.py, tests/test_skill_contract_parity.py) keep their base failing ids and add none.

The manifest writes baseline_suite and after_suite each as one line of armed JSON: revision, command with no placeholder, exit_status, completed, failure_count, failure_ids, log_path. node_definition.done_when:
Promotion consults reckon/crew/standing_suite.py:hold_reason. When a run's review tier is none or light and hold_reason returns a sentence for the owning project, reckon crew complete refuses, naming that sentence and the two ways out: record a passing suite run, or record a lead waiver with standing_suite.record_waiver. A full-tier promotion is never held by it. The check is made where promotion already resolves the tier, near reckon/crew/promotion.py:_require_review_waiver. It reads the project root and name promotion already has, and it neither copies nor re-derives the tier.

Two commands in reckon/cli.py:
- reckon crew suite run --project NAME runs the project's declared suite through standing_suite.run under its budget and records the result with standing_suite.record, printing the recorded counts as JSON.
- reckon crew suite waive --project NAME --reason TEXT records a waiver.

tests/test_standing_suite_holds_promotion.py synthesises a project under tmp_path whose declared suite fails at collection, then records a run. It drives the promotion path the other promotion tests use and asserts:
- a tier-none promotion is refused with the hold sentence;
- a full-tier promotion is not held;
- after a later passing run, or a recorded waiver, the tier-none promotion proceeds.
It reads and writes nothing outside tmp_path. That file, tests/test_standing_suite.py and the existing promotion test files keep their base failing ids and add none. For promotion.py, the population is the full tests/ directory, run with -n 8; its FAILED ids are compared with base in the same environment and none are added.

The manifest writes baseline_suite and after_suite each as one line of armed JSON: revision, command with no placeholder, exit_status, completed, failure_count, failure_ids, log_path. Every gate log opens with one line naming its revision, tree and command. The declared negative control is applied and observed to fail, and its log's absolute path is in the manifest with an EXIT= line and the FAILED id.
node_definition.goal: Make promotion hold tier none and light promotions while the project's declared suite last failed to collect or overran its budget, and give the coordinator commands to run and record the suite and to waive the hold

It uses a temporary repository with 50 registered worktrees and a git shim on PATH that counts status calls, and it drives the crew complete entry point. A fenced run's snapshot holds 2 trees, its own worktree and the main checkout, and its promotion makes 2 status calls. An unfenced run's snapshot holds 51 trees, and its promotion makes 51. node_definition.done_when: the follow read loop in reckon/crew/runs.py never parses or advances past a final line that lacks its newline. Only _follow_boundary changes in reckon/cli.py. A new tests/test_follow_reads_whole_lines.py starts the real follow loop, writes half a record, lets the loop read, completes the record, and asserts it is delivered exactly once with its full content. A second case asserts _follow_boundary reads no more than a bounded number of bytes on a stream larger than 1 MB. The declared mutation, accepting a line without its newline, fails the first case with its log recorded including an EXIT= line. node_definition.done_when: tests/test_dispatch_places_into_the_shared_reservation.py passes under the root .venv python. It runs in a temporary RECKON_HOME against a recording scheduler; no real sbatch, salloc, srun or scancel runs. Four cases. (1) A dispatch declaring placement, with no published reservation, reaches ensure_reservation from placement resolution in reckon/crew/dispatch.py. It holds the shared allocation, publishes it to the unkeyed record, and runs its worker as a step inside it with --overlap and the job id just published. (2) A second dispatch under a different project reads that same record, starts no allocation of its own, and runs its worker as a step in the allocation it found. Across both dispatches the recording scheduler logs exactly one allocation-obtaining request; the two step launches are not counted. (3) A backend declaring no placement is untouched: no ensure call, no request, and wrapping unchanged. (4) A legacy per-project record, the shape of placement/imas-ambix/reservation.json, is still honoured: its job id is placed into, and no hold is made. tests/test_crew_placement_reservation.py::test_an_unheld_reservation_leaves_the_declared_wrapping_unchanged is replaced by a test whose name states the ensure. The retry assertion in tests/test_ensure_holds_one_reservation.py asserts a literal attempt count that fails if _UNKNOWN_PROBE_ATTEMPTS is reduced to 1, instead of reading the module constant. The declared negative control is executed and logged. The test files importing reckon.crew.dispatch or reckon.crew.placement show 0 added failures between a base arm and a head arm, run with pytest-xdist -n 8, each arm with its own --basetemp under /tmp deleted afterwards. Stop and log df if /tmp has under 5 GB free. Every log sits under the run directory, headed with revision, tree and command and ending EXIT=. Out of scope, listed as follow_ons: adopting 1277272, and placement on the crew resume path.

node_definition.done_when: tests/test_a_live_worker_never_reads_gone_after_its_first_commit.py drives a stub worker in a temporary RECKON_HOME. The stub's recorded pid stays alive while one commit is made in its worktree beyond the run's base. The test then runs the live classifier and the producer's transition over that pointer. It asserts that no emitted transition reads "the worker process is gone" or classifies blocked with recovery resume while the pid is alive. It also asserts that the transition and the live classifier agree the worker is alive. At the node's base, the test is run and its result logged. If it passes at base, the manifest names the commit that removed the defect f-acpewio-first-commit-gone describes, with the evidence; 7bcd27ac0 is the candidate. In that case no product file changes. If it fails at base, the fix lands in reckon/crew/recovery.py, in the branches that write "the worker process is gone with no recorded exit" (around :4860 to :4875), so that the recorded pid's liveness decides, and the test passes. The declared negative control is executed and logged: in a scratch tree, make that classification treat the worker as dead whenever its worktree carries a commit, and the test fails. The test files that import reckon.crew.recovery are run at base and at head with pytest-xdist -n 8, each arm with its own --basetemp under /tmp, and they add no failing id. Every log sits under the run directory, headed with revision, tree and literal command, and ends EXIT=. Basetemps are deleted afterwards. Only the new test file and, if needed, reckon/crew/recovery.py change.

node_definition.done_when: No real scheduler verb runs in this node. Every case uses a recording scheduler on PATH in a temporary RECKON_HOME, and no allocation is submitted, adopted, cancelled or reloaded for real. The locked decision in f-tfsoa-handoff-01 is that the one shared allocation is the supervisor-running kind: an ambix-fleet or reckon-fleet batch job whose batch step runs fleet-supervisor, found by reckon/crew/fleet_node.py find_allocation and its job comment. The node builds on fleet_node.py and does not add a second hold path beside it. After the change, ensure_reservation, given no unkeyed record while fleet_node finds a live supervisor-running allocation, publishes that job to the unkeyed record at crew_home()/placement/reservation.json with the allocation's own declared shape (partition, cores, memory) read from the scheduler. It then submits nothing, and reports the job as adopted. With a record naming that job and a live probe, it reports already-held and submits nothing. With neither, it keeps its present hold behaviour. A resumed run is placed too: the crew resume launch path (reckon/crew/resumption.py and dispatch.resume_plan at reckon/crew/dispatch.py:8118) resolves placement through resolve_backend_placement exactly as dispatch does, so a resumed worker of a placement-declaring backend runs as a step with --overlap in the published job. tests/test_the_fleet_allocation_is_adopted.py asserts four things against the recording scheduler. First, one adoption from a recorded supervisor-running job with zero allocation-obtaining requests and the record naming that job id. Second, a second ensure under another project reading the same job with zero requests. Third, a resumed run placed as a step in the adopted job. Fourth, a backend declaring no placement untouched on resume. The declared negative control is executed and logged: remove the adoption branch in a scratch tree, and the first case logs one allocation-obtaining request and fails. The test files importing reckon.crew.placement, reckon.crew.fleet_node or reckon.crew.resumption are run at base and at head with pytest-xdist -n 8, each arm with its own --basetemp under /tmp, and they add no failing id. The comment at reckon/crew/placement.py around :344 that still says the project is carried in the path is corrected. node_definition.done_when: First reproduce at base: a review whose finding reads FINDING tests/test_x.py:12 blocking: the guard never fires parses to exactly the keys file, line and text (the currency report at /home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/reports/reckon/s22-coord/scoring-currency/report.md shows the call). Then the vocabulary is declared once, as a module-level constant the prompt text and the parser both read, with at most three values, one of them the blocking value; reckon/crew/prompts/review.md tells a reviewer how to mark a finding with it. The parser records a severity only when the finding states one of the declared values, leaves the field absent otherwise, and keeps file, line and text unchanged for every finding shape it parsed before. A stored review record round-trips the field through the production reader. A new tests/test_a_finding_says_whether_it_blocks.py asserts each declared value parses, an undeclared word stays in the text with no severity, a finding with no severity has no severity key, existing finding shapes parse exactly as before, and the prompt names every declared value. The named negative control (the parser ignores severity) reddens the blocking case. The gate is that new test plus tests/test_review_findings_compose_a_repair.py, tests/test_readers_compose_the_record.py and tests/test_review_composition.py, run at base and at head. Each arm is recorded as JSON carrying completed true and a literal command with absolute paths and no angle-bracket placeholder; each log names its revision on the first line and ends with a bare line reading EXIT= followed by the exit code. Every pytest process uses a basetemp private to that process. The head arm adds no failure id; any added id means status blocked, naming each id. ruff check and ruff format --check over the changed paths report no finding the base did not. Scratch goes under /tmp in a directory named for this run and is deleted before status complete, printed and listed in artifacts. An evidence fragment at docs/evidence/fragments/scoring-should-stop-a-promotion/a-finding-says-whether-it-blocks.html records the change and the vocabulary. The turn ends once the manifest reads complete or blocked.

node_definition.done_when: First reproduce at base: with the local lane declaring a lane_document that reads running 30 against concurrent_requests 22 with a fresh observed_at, _review_lane_candidates still puts that lane first (the currency report at /home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/reports/reckon/s22-coord/scoring-currency/report.md shows the call). Then a lane whose own document is fresh (observed_at within 45 seconds of now) and reports running at or above concurrent_requests is treated as saturated. A saturated local lane holds the review as awaiting-lane, with a reason naming the lane and its running and ceiling figures; it never hands the review to a metered lane instead, because local-lane-shaped work stays on the local lane. The document's drained shape reads as open, not saturated: at running 0 it carries headroom null, sizing_verdict do-not-size and no concurrent_requests key, only concurrent_requests_instant. A document that is stale, unreadable or absent reads as unknown and changes nothing, so a missing reading never holds a review. A new tests/test_a_review_waits_for_a_saturated_lane.py covers the saturated case (held, reason names the figures, no pointer created), the healthy case (the local lane still leads), the drained shape (open), a stale document (unchanged ordering) and an absent document (unchanged ordering). The named negative control (ignore the lane document) reddens the saturated case. The gate is that new test plus tests/test_review_reflex_selects_a_backend.py, tests/test_rereview_keeps_its_lane.py, tests/test_review_lane_follows_its_run.py, tests/test_a_review_never_runs_in_harness.py, tests/test_review_reflex_sweep.py and tests/test_a_repair_hold_names_its_cause.py, run at base and at head. Each arm is recorded as JSON carrying completed true and a literal command with absolute paths and no angle-bracket placeholder; each log names its revision on the first line and ends with a bare line reading EXIT= followed by the exit code. Every pytest process uses a basetemp private to that process. The head arm adds no failure id; any added id means status blocked, naming each id. ruff check and ruff format --check over the changed paths report no finding the base did not. Scratch goes under /tmp in a directory named for this run and is deleted before status complete, printed and listed in artifacts. node_definition.done_when: A CLI worker's dispatch is refused before any worktree, live pointer or run directory exists in two cases: bwrap is absent from PATH, or a user namespace cannot be created. The refusal's error and detail name the missing capability: bwrap not found, or the namespace probe's own failure text. reckon crew dispatch --no-fence REASON launches the same dispatch unfenced. The reason is recorded on the live pointer, in the composed launch plan, and on the run's ledger row at promotion. A run dispatched without the flag records no such field, and a dispatch whose fence composes normally is unchanged. tests/test_the_fence_fails_closed.py drives these cases in a temporary RECKON_HOME with a stub backend. 1: PATH without bwrap is refused naming bwrap, and no worktree, pointer or run directory is left. 2: a namespace probe forced to fail is refused naming the namespace. 3: --no-fence with a reason launches, and the pointer carries the reason. 4: promoting that run writes the reason onto its ledger row. 5: an ordinary fenced dispatch is unchanged. 6: where bwrap can run, a fenced stub's write into a sibling run's worktree fails as a read-only file system while its write into its own worktree lands; where bwrap cannot run, the case skips, and its skip reason names the capability. The declared negative control is executed and logged: in a scratch tree, make the capability check report success when bwrap is absent, and case 1 fails. The test files importing reckon.crew.dispatch or reckon._backends are run at base and at head with pytest-xdist -n 8, each arm with its own --basetemp under /tmp, and they add no failing id. Every log sits under the run directory, headed with revision, tree and literal command, and ends EXIT=, and basetemps are deleted afterwards. Only reckon/crew/dispatch.py, reckon/cli.py, reckon/_backends.py, reckon/crew/promotion.py and the new test file change. If the ledger row needs reckon/ledger.py, the manifest names that change under follow_ons rather than making it.

node_definition.done_when: No real scheduler verb runs at any point in this node. Every pytest run has, first on PATH, a shim directory under the run directory holding salloc, sbatch, srun, squeue, scontrol and scancel stubs. Each stub appends its argv and its caller's PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST to a log under the run directory, then exits non-zero. `squeue -u $USER -h -o '%i %j %M'` is logged before and after every run, and no job named reckon-reservation appears. First, the tests that reach a scheduler through dispatch are named. The candidate files are run one at a time under the shim: tests/test_dispatch_places_into_the_shared_reservation.py, tests/test_crew_placement.py, tests/test_crew_lane_agnostic_placement.py, tests/test_crew_workspace_requirements.py, tests/test_crew.py, tests/test_flight.py, tests/test_capabilities.py, tests/test_crew_binding_bound.py, tests/test_concurrency_bound_refuses_by_name.py and tests/test_landing_contract_follows_the_grant.py. The manifest lists every test id whose run logged a salloc or sbatch call, with the call path from dispatch to ensure_reservation at file and line in reckon/crew/dispatch.py and reckon/crew/placement.py. It also says why the recording scheduler that test already uses, if any, did not intercept the call. Five real allocations were minted this way on 2026-09-30, one per whole-suite run, each with partition all, 32 CPUs, 128 GB and an unlimited time limit. The fix has two parts. First, each named test gives its dispatch a recording scheduler, or a placement that never reaches the real one, and keeps its assertion. Second, tests/conftest.py fails any test that reaches a scheduler verb the test did not provide, and the failure names the verb and its argv. The check puts a failing stub first on PATH for the whole session, and a test's own recording scheduler, prepended later, still takes precedence. After the fix, the whole suite is run once with pytest-xdist -n 8, the shim in place and a per-test --basetemp under /tmp. The shim log records no salloc or sbatch call. Every failing id at head also fails at base, or the manifest attributes it. The negative control is executed and logged under the shim: with one named test's fix reverted in a scratch tree, the conftest check fails that test, naming salloc. No assertion is deleted. Every log sits under the run directory, headed with revision, tree and literal command, and ends EXIT=, and basetemps are deleted afterwards. tests/test_crew.py is run but not edited, because other nodes hold it. If a test there reaches a scheduler, the manifest names it under follow_ons with the one-line fix it needs, and the full-suite arm lists it as attributed. Only tests/conftest.py and the other named test files change, and the manifest lists which of them it edited.

node_definition.done_when: First reproduce at base: a promotion whose record fails two independent preconditions (for example an unmoved impl together with a passing gate missing its log) is refused for only the first, and the second appears only on a second call; record it as the base arm. Design constraint: preconditions that can be judged independently are evaluated together and reported in one CrewError, listed in the order the sequence checks them today, with the first one's existing wording kept first, so a caller matching on the first refusal still matches. A precondition that cannot be judged until an earlier one holds (for example, one that reads a manifest the earlier check found unreadable) stays sequential, and the manifest says which ones those are and why. When the stored review read a head the manifest's commits do not name, the refusal names that reviewed head as the commit to pass. In a new tests/test_one_refusal_lists_every_precondition.py: one call against a record failing two independent preconditions raises once, naming both; a record failing one precondition raises with its wording unchanged; and the reviewed-head case names the head to cite. The named negative control (the aggregation reverted so the first failure raises alone) is executed and fails the two-precondition case. Measure fallout before declaring complete: run every test file under tests/ that calls crew complete, complete(), or _complete_locked, or matches a promotion refusal, at base and at head, and list them in the manifest. Any id that fails only at head because it asserted the old one-refusal shape is reported by id with status blocked, rather than edited outside the fence. Each arm is recorded as JSON carrying completed true and a literal command with absolute paths and no angle-bracket placeholder; each log names its revision on the first line and ends with a bare line reading EXIT= followed by the exit code. Run each arm with -n 8 and --timeout=300, each process on a basetemp under /tmp private to it. ruff check and ruff format --check over the changed Python paths report no finding the base did not. Scratch goes under /tmp in a directory named for this run and is deleted before status complete. An evidence fragment at docs/evidence/fragments/scoring-should-stop-a-promotion/one-refusal-lists-every-precondition.html records the change. node_definition.done_when: Measured 2026-10-01 09:10 CEST: with host-layer placement declared for clive (options ["--ntasks=1"]), every clive dispatch was refused with "partition admitted cores bound (20 of 1 cores admitted (1 per worker))". At reckon/crew/summary.py:309, cores_bound reads --ntasks from the placement options as the cores the whole reservation admits, but --ntasks there is the shape of one step. Its occupancy is every live pointer on the backend, placed or not, some days old. After the change, a placement that places into the shared reservation takes its admitted cores from the published reservation record (crew_home()/placement/reservation.json, size.cores, read through reckon/crew/placement.py read_reservation). The per-worker share comes from --cpus-per-task or -c in the options, defaulting to 1. --ntasks is never read as the admitted size. Three parts, all in the unresolvable-commit region of reckon/crew/promotion.py on your base, which is current main.

Part one ports run r-20261001T051714453460-one-refusal-lists-every-precondition. Its commits are 5bfd82b52c98bf09bedda6ea6c00922df1b082af and e0434c29b88a58ce92e54fbc53deadb9722d1f47; read them with git show. They no longer merge, because main's complete() changed in the same region at ee3f37084 and b4233a9cb. Re-implement them on your base:
- crew complete reports every independently judgeable precondition in one refusal, with the first one's wording first;
- the stored-review refusal names the reviewed head to cite;
- cited revisions are canonicalised through _resolve_commits, so the ledger row records full shas;
- main's reconcile behaviour stays intact.

Part two fixes a regression on main that started when a399d7744 made the presented branch refuse unresolvable values. A review run whose commits field is a commitless declaration in prose (for example: none, review node, no repository change, the review is the deliverable) is now refused as an unresolvable presented commit. A commitless declaration that the existing declaration parser recognises means no commits. A word that only begins with an absence word is still not a declaration.

Part three gives one vocabulary to every unresolvable-commit refusal: presented, declared and resolver. Today tests/test_crew.py::test_promotion_refuses_a_commit_that_names_no_object expects 'does not resolve to a commit object', and tests/test_commitless_review_promotes.py expects 'does not resolve to an object'. Choose one, and update whichever test pins the superseded wording, giving the reason in the commit message.

Before changing anything, record the base arm at current main: tests/test_commitless_review_promotes.py has 4 failures (test_a_report_only_review_promotes_over_its_own_deliverable, test_a_review_with_commits_prose_promotes_on_a_clean_worktree, test_an_implement_run_whose_commits_do_not_resolve_is_refused, test_a_word_that_only_begins_with_an_absence_word_is_not_a_declaration).

At head, those four pass, along with:
- tests/test_crew.py::test_promotion_refuses_a_commit_that_names_no_object;
- tests/test_cited_identifier_resolves.py;
- tests/test_one_refusal_on_main.py, which carries over the cases of tests/test_one_refusal_lists_every_precondition.py from e0434c29b, adapted to main;
- tests/test_control_gate_repairs.py, tests/test_a_short_commit_list_is_reported.py and tests/test_gate_evidence.py.

Execute two named controls and record each log: with the aggregation reverted, the two-precondition case fails; with the commitless-declaration check removed from the presented branch, the report-only review case fails.

Evidence rules:
- Each arm is recorded as JSON carrying completed true and a literal command with absolute paths and no angle-bracket placeholder.
- Each log names its revision on the first line and ends with a bare line reading EXIT= followed by the exit code.

Scratch goes under /tmp in a directory named for this run and is deleted before status complete. An evidence fragment at docs/evidence/fragments/scoring-should-stop-a-promotion/one-refusal-on-main.html records the port, the regression fix and the chosen vocabulary. The turn ends once the manifest reads complete or blocked.

node_definition.done_when: The the-suite-is-green-at-head followup f-sgh-shared-basetemp-destroys-a-peer holds. s22's measurement is at ~/.config/reckon/crew/reports/reckon/s22-coord/reflex-tests-environment/report.md. A pytest session given an explicit --basetemp takes a lock beside it (a file next to the basetemp directory, not inside it, since pytest removes and recreates the directory) and holds it for the whole session. A second session starting on the same basetemp while a live pid holds the lock is refused before pytest removes anything, and the refusal names the holding pid and the basetemp. A stale lock whose pid is dead is taken over. A sequential second session on the same basetemp starts normally. tests/conftest.py carries this as a session-scoped hook. tests/test_a_shared_basetemp_is_refused.py drives three cases, each with two child pytest processes in a temporary directory outside any repository. 1: the second session is refused naming the first's pid, and the first session's fixture files are intact afterwards. 2: a session started after the first has exited runs normally on the same basetemp. 3: a lock left by a dead pid is taken over. The declared negative control is executed and logged under pytest: remove the lock in a scratch tree, and case 1's second session deletes the first's fixture directory, so the case fails. tests/conftest.py's existing session checks (the scheduler guard and the producer reaper) keep their behaviour. The test files under tests/ are run at base and at head with pytest-xdist -n 8, each arm with its own --basetemp under $TMPDIR, and they add no failing id. Every log sits under the run directory, headed with revision, tree and literal command, and ends EXIT=. Only tests/conftest.py and the new test file change.

node_definition.done_when: a-dispatch-returns-without-its-worker §6's done-when holds. tests/test_dispatch_result_matches_launch.py drives a dispatch with a stub backend in a temporary crew config home, through each path the section names that has returned a refusal beside a live pointer. It covers the handler around the post-launch tree snapshot, imas-ambix-61's post-launch cleanup that refused to remove the run's own worktree, and the survival-check refusal removed at merge 1859c0d19, which stays as a regression guard. For each, the test asserts that the result either names the launched run with ok: true, or leaves no pointer, no worktree for the node, and no worker that record_process_alive reports alive. A refusal that leaves any one of the three fails the test. At the node's base, each mechanism is driven first and the manifest states whether it still returns a refusal beside a pointer, a worktree or a live worker, naming the commit that removed it if it no longer does. A second test passes an unresolvable --member and asserts a refusal with no auto-derived member bound; this verifies existing behaviour and changes no source. A third test covers every ok: false result the reckon crew dispatch command emits, live and --dry-run alike, including a contract-validation refusal on a done-when holding a literal placeholder. It asserts each carries error and detail as non-empty strings, so an absent key fails as a null one does. Any refusal missing them is fixed, in reckon/cli.py (the dry-run verdict and the not-dispatchable branch) or reckon/crew/dispatch.py. The declared negative control is executed and logged under pytest at the base, wherever a refusal is returned beside a live pointer, or else by removing one fix in a scratch tree. node_definition.done_when: a-crew-process-ends-with-its-owner §9's done-when, as released at bd3db958d, holds. A backend may declare gate_document in flight config, and every dispatch whose resolved backend declares it reads the gate before creating a pointer or worktree, whether --local or --backend chose that backend. Each result carries lane_gate with the state the section's five-state rule names. A dispatch that waits returns ok false with error lane-paused, creates no pointer and no worktree, and the reckon crew dispatch command exits 75. The follower's review reflex, dispatch_review_for_run in reckon/crew/recovery.py, launches nothing while the gate waits, and its report row carries error lane-paused and the reason. A declared gate_document that differs from the lane document's published router_generation_gate.config_path waits, naming both paths, and a lane document that publishes no config_path or cannot be read within its own 5 s deadline records lane_gate.path_check as skipped. tests/test_dispatch_holds_while_the_lane_is_paused.py, in a temporary RECKON_HOME with a stub local backend, a temporary gate file and a stub lane document, drives every bullet of the section's done-when list and asserts lane_gate.state in each result. The declared negative control is executed and logged under pytest: with the gate check removed, the paused dispatch creates a pointer and the test fails. The _dispatch_lane_reading docstring names both facts that withhold a dispatch. The manifest names the flight-config schema file before editing it, and the generated reckon/_flight_schema.py and docs/_shared/flight.schema.json are regenerated by the generator b705f792f used. The node gate is the new test file at head, ending EXIT=0. No real gate file, lane document or scheduler is read or written. Every log sits under the run directory, headed with revision, tree and literal command, and ends EXIT=. Only reckon/crew/dispatch.py, reckon/crew/recovery.py, reckon/cli.py (the dispatch command's exit status), reckon/schema/flight.yaml, reckon/_flight_schema.py, docs/_shared/flight.schema.json and the new test file change.
